title: Stop drawing a green check on an unwritten asset target
body:
## Summary
AssetTarget and the generic gallery panel render a green check beside a path nothing has written.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/steps/shared/assetHonesty.tsx:70 documents that an asset path is a target and never evidence that a file exists, then line 74 renders it with a check mark in t.ok. src/components/layout-lab/steps/ArchetypeStep.tsx:513 renders the same wording, and ArchetypeStepGalleryAssetTarget.test.tsx:53 pins it. Fixing one side forks the claim between the bespoke and generic paths, so both must move together. Fixed looks like a neutral arrow glyph in t.muted on both, with the test re-pinned.

## Flow
- Open a produced gallery step in stub mode
- The Selected panel shows a green check and the UE path
- No file exists at that path until the drain runs

## Expected impact
Operators stop reading a target as a delivered file. The wording is pinned by one test, which must be re-pinned.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a target no longer reads as a delivered asset
Before: 2 render sites draw a check in the ok colour for an unwritten path
After: 0 sites predicted
Method: simulation - 2 sites read; not built because src/components/layout-lab/steps/ArchetypeStep.tsx is outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Render test over AssetTarget and the ArchetypeStep gallery panel asserting no check glyph and no ok colour on the target line

title: Stop the bar track opacity dimming every ChartPanel fill
body:
## Summary
The bars variant puts opacity 0.4 on the track that contains the fill, so every fill renders at 40% or less.

## Description
In src/components/layout-lab/steps/shared/ChartPanel.tsx BarsChart the track div carries opacity 0.4 and the motion fill is its child, and CSS opacity composes. A highlight row asks for opacity 1 and gets 0.4; a normal row asks for 0.85 and gets 0.34. Highlight and caller colours are washed out by the same factor. Fixed looks like the track tint on a sibling or background layer, leaving the fill at its requested opacity.

## Flow
- Render a bars chart with a highlight row
- Read effective alpha as the product of fill and track opacity
- Effective alpha is 0.4 where the code asks for 1

## Expected impact
Every budget chart gains contrast. It changes the look of all bars charts, so an operator should see it before it lands.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - bar fills reach their requested opacity
Before: effective alpha 0.40 highlight, 0.34 normal
After: 1.00 highlight, 0.85 normal predicted
Method: simulation - computed from the styles; a real render is needed to judge the look
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/layout-lab/steps/shared/ChartPanel.tsx BarsChart: track style opacity 0.4 wraps the motion.div fill with opacity r.highlight ? 1 : 0.85
instrument: Style assertion that no ancestor of the fill sets opacity, plus a before and after screenshot of one bars step

title: Measure whether GlbViewer leaks meshes through the useGLTF cache
body:
## Summary
GlbViewer loads every browsed mesh through useGLTF and never clears it.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/steps/shared/GlbViewer.tsx Model calls useGLTF(url), which caches parsed scenes per url for the page lifetime, and nothing calls useGLTF.clear or disposes geometry. Browsing a 3D gallery may therefore retain every mesh viewed. This is unmeasured: the size of the retention has not been taken, and clearing a url still in use elsewhere could break another viewer.

## Flow
- Open a 3D gallery step
- Select several real meshes in turn
- Compare JS heap and renderer.info.memory after each selection

## Expected impact
Long browsing sessions would hold less memory if retention is real. Clearing too eagerly forces a re-download or breaks a second viewer.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - browsed meshes are released
Before: not measured; 0 clear or dispose calls in the file
After: not measured
Method: simulation - read only; needs real WebGL, which jsdom lacks
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/layout-lab/steps/shared/GlbViewer.tsx Model: useGLTF(url) with no useGLTF.clear or dispose in the file
instrument: Browser probe logging renderer.info.memory and JS heap across 20 mesh selections, with and without clearing on url change
